name: PL-8177
lead: PL-8177 is an investigational oral peptide agonist of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1r). [1][2] It has been studied for inflammatory conditions, not for tanning or pigmentation: preclinical work with PL-8177 and PL-8331 examined prevention and reversal of intestinal and ocular inflammation in animal models. [1]
A phase 2a trial in active ulcerative colitis (n=16) began in September 2022. [2] No studies were found of PL-8177 for skin pigmentation or appearance.
infobox: Ulcerative colitis; preclinical ocular and intestinal inflammation

paras: NCT05466890 is a phase 2a study in active ulcerative colitis (n=16, active not recruiting). [2] A 2018 paper reported preclinical studies in animal models. [1] No studies were found in pigmentation or cosmetic use.

timeline.event: Preclinical study of MC1r agonists PL-8177 and PL-8331 published. [1]

card.note: Investigational; its studied purpose is inflammation, not pigment.

quick.overview:
PL-8177 is an experimental oral peptide that activates the melanocortin 1 receptor, the same receptor family linked to skin pigmentation.

Its published and registered research concerns inflammation, including a small ulcerative colitis trial.
quick.mechanism: It mimics alpha-MSH at MC1r, which in animal models reduced intestinal and ocular inflammation.
quick.risks: Not approved; human safety data are limited to early-phase trials.
